_what_this_is: Adversarial regressions for the one-time genesis authority and for semantic competence.
Genesis exists because the PR that rewrites the trust root cannot be certified by that trust
root, and because a candidate that authors its own standard can meet a weak one honestly.
These mutations attack the boundary: the external policy defines what must be proven, the
candidate manifest may only describe the tree, observations are read from a real run's log,
and the human creates the authorization.

defects.why: The candidate could silently edit the very verifier that certifies its new trust root.
A genesis policy the human never reviewed could define the standard genesis is judged by.

defects.find: policy_path.is_absolute() and repo not in policy_path.parents,
defects.replace: True or (policy_path.is_absolute() and repo not in policy_path.parents),
defects.why: The candidate could supply the external genesis policy from inside its own repository.
A genesis manifest the human never reviewed could describe the trust root being authorized.
The one-time genesis exception could be applied to a commit other than the one named.
The candidate could author its own evidence minimums or assert its own authorization.

defects.find: narrowed = [p for p in policy["required_trust_root_prefixes"] if p not in prefixes]
defects.why: The candidate could narrow the trust-root scope so a whole authority family escapes the inventory.

defects.find: absent_paths = [p for p in policy["required_trust_root_paths"] if p not in files]
defects.why: The candidate could omit a mandatory trust-root file from the genesis inventory.

defects.find: absent_policies = [p for p in policy["required_policy_files"] if p not in policies]
defects.why: The candidate could omit a governing policy file from the hashes pinned at genesis.

defects.find: covered = [p for p in prefixes if MANIFEST == p or MANIFEST.startswith(p)]
defects.why: The manifest could fall inside its own hashed prefix, where no fixed point exists.
Validation of the parent commit could be presented as exact-head evidence for the manifest-bearing child.
An arbitrary log could be substituted for the one the evidence document commits to.
Evidence from some other run could be accepted as the run the human named at ceremony time.
A validation result measured against a different commit could authorize this one.

defects.find: absent = sorted({s for s in mandatory if s not in names})
defects.why: A mandatory stage, holdout class or external requirement could be omitted from the run entirely.
Genesis could be authorized on measurements weaker than the external policy demands.

defects.find: require(caught == total, f"observed {family} let a mutation escape")
defects.replace: require(True, f"observed {family} let a mutation escape")
defects.why: Genesis could be authorized on evidence in which trust-root mutations escaped.
A whole mutation family could be omitted from the genesis evidence.

defects.find: if not all(str(value or "").strip() for value in supplied):
defects.replace: if False and not all(str(value or "").strip() for value in supplied):
defects.why: The out-of-band human anchor could be omitted entirely, leaving the candidate to certify itself.
The factory's own detector tests could be weakened by an ordinary PR without tripping the trust-root guard.
An authority could certify a claim it is never shown the artifacts for: independent, but not competent.
A validation result that says it failed would still authorize genesis.

defects.find: require(not (result.get("failed_stages") or []), "validation result reports failed stages")
defects.why: A result listing failed stages but carrying a pass verdict would be accepted.
A provisional calibration run, whose stages only printed the driver digests, would authorize genesis.
